main_body: Japanese townhouse front: a tall tile roof, a white plaster band, a lower eave roof, then a dark timber lattice wall with a recessed doorway and straw bundles
top_band: x=32: rows 1-5 grey-blue ridge band (L 158/130/83/130/83), then a dark row at 6. It reads as a thin ridge cap, not a surface seen from above. Rows 7-28 are vertical tile stripes, the same family as the face.
evidence: The whole drawing is a straight-on elevation. The roof is a flat field of vertical tile stripes with no top slope receding from a ridge and no visible hip faces. The plaster band, lower eave and lattice wall (rows 50-76) are all vertical faces with no horizontal surface seen from above. The lattice bars and doorway are painted flat, with no inset edges or eave shadow. Only the ridge strip at the top (rows 1-5) hints at a top, and it is too thin and flat to count. The result is a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The candidate has 7 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, and 33 distinct colours against 185 and 66. 72% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline is the near-black sticker look instead of a dark tone of the adjacent material. The roof tiles are repeated vertical stripes with about 4 tones and no per-tile highlights or scallops. The plaster band and the wooden lattice are simple repeated patterns. Flat-fill coverage is low (3%), but the piece is clearly thinner and more schematic than the Beodeul houses.
